Issues.Title: RichEdit gets slower with every edit after a UI Automation client touches it (Windows 11)
Issues.Body:
Once a UI Automation client has read any property from a RichEdit control, msftedit keeps a text-range object for every later change to the control and never frees them. Every change walks the whole list, so the cost of an edit grows with the number of edits made since the touch. The client going away makes no difference, and nothing the application can do resets it short of restarting the process.

One property read is enough, and any UI Automation client qualifies: Narrator or another screen reader, a dictation tool, a UI test driver, or an inspection tool such as Inspect or Accessibility Insights. Clients that use the older MSAA interface do not trigger it, and neither does plain Win32 access to the window.

Seen on Windows 11 24H2 and later (`msftedit.dll` 10.0.26100.9711), in both .NET Framework 4.8 and .NET 10 WinForms applications. An application affected on Windows 11 shows no slowdown on Windows 10. The symptom is UI-thread CPU, not memory: the objects are small, but after tens of thousands of edits each one costs tens of milliseconds, and an operation that makes a few hundred edits takes tens of seconds. A long-running application that edits a RichEdit programmatically can become unusable over a working day once an automation client has touched it.


### Steps to reproduce

Repro app: https://github.com/dhimmel/richedit-uia-leak-repro (.NET 10 WinForms, one `RichTextBox`, driver and client scripts in PowerShell).

Issues.Title: [release/11.0] Fix clipboard stalls during delayed rendering
Issues.Body: Backport of #15346 to release/11.0 /cc @Shyam-Gupta @davkean ## Issue Clipboard operations can stall and fail with `CLIPBRD_E_CANT_OPEN`. In a Visual Studio trace, Windows Clipboard User Service (`cbdhsvc`) was reading data through OLE and blocked in the delayed-rendering path: ```text CClipDataObject::GetData -> GetClipboardData -> xxxGetRenderData -> xxxInterSendMsgEx ``` ## Root Cause Windows was synchronously requesting clipboard data from the editor's UI thread (`WM_RENDERFORMAT`), while the service held the clipboard open. That UI thread was trying to replace the clipboard contents and sleeping between failed open attempts, so it could not answer the render request until retries were exhausted. ## Fix The retry wait now lets the UI thread answer sent messages, breaking that dependency without processing posted messages or queued input. Retry intervals and attempt limits remain unchanged. ## Customer Impact Clipboard operations in WinForms and WPF can recover from this contention instead of exhausting retries. ## Regression? Since .NET 11, WinForms runtime repo has started shipping an internal NuGet package, targeting .NET Framework, which includes the shared Clipboard and the new NRBF serializer/deserializer (the BinaryFormatter replacement). This package is consumed by VS AppLocal WPF which is shipped with VS and handles the Clipboard operations. This bug got introduced as part of that new package. Till Dev17, the Clipboard was handled by the old WPF code which didn’t have this issue. So, it can be considered as a regression. ## Risk All pending sent messages can run, not just clipboard-render requests. Their handlers can reenter application code and change clipboard or UI state. The retry deadline does not bound time spent inside a handler. ## Test methodology Mock OLE operations and private windows cover all five retry paths, delayed rendering, unrelated sent messages, nested calls, retry exhaustion, and posted-message preservation without touching the system clipboard. Also manually tested this with Visual Studio by continually holding down CTRL+X. ### Before ### After ## Test environment(s) Windows x64; .NET Framework 4.8.1 (x64 and x86) and .NET 12 (x64). ###### Microsoft Reviewers: [Open in CodeFlow](https://microsoft.github.io/open-pr/?codeflow=https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/15371)

Issues.Title: Fix Image.Width/Height DefaultValue (false -> 0) for dotnet/runtime#126265
Issues.Body:
Fixes dotnet/runtime#126265

## Proposed changes

**What:** Change `DefaultValue` metadata for `System.Drawing.Image.Width` and `System.Drawing.Image.Height` from `DefaultValue(false)` to `DefaultValue(0)`.

**Why:** `Width`/`Height` are `int` properties but declared `[DefaultValue(false)]`. Metadata consumers that read the default via `TypeDescriptor`/`PropertyDescriptor.Attributes` receive a `Boolean` value. When `Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi` (or `System.Text.Json.Schema.JsonSchema`) generates a schema from a model containing an `Image?` property, it does `UnboxOnWrite<int>(defaultValue)` and throws:

```
InvalidCastException: Unable to cast object of type 'System.Boolean' to type 'System.Int32'.
  at System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.UnboxOnWrite<T>(object value)
  at Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi.JsonNodeSchemaExtensions.ApplyDefaultValue(...)
```

This is the exact failure reported in dotnet/runtime#126265.

**How:**
- `src/System.Drawing.Common/src/System/Drawing/Image.cs`: `Width`/`Height` `[DefaultValue(false)]` → `[DefaultValue(0)]`.
- `src/System.Drawing.Common/src/Special/NotSupported.cs` (netstandard stub): same fix for the two stub properties.
- `src/System.Drawing.Common/tests/System/Drawing/ImageTests.cs`: add `ImageDimensionProperty_DefaultValueIsZero` theory asserting `TypeDescriptor` default is `(int)0` for both properties.
- `src/System.Drawing.Common/src/CompatibilitySuppressions.xml`: intentional `CP0015` suppressions for both properties across `net10.0`/`netstandard2.0` baselines (`[T:System.ComponentModel.DefaultValueAttribute]` target).

> **Duplicate note:** Draft PR #14895 (`Fix Image dimension DefaultValue metadata`, https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/pull/14895) covers the same issue and was verified present before opening this PR. This PR is opened per contributor request as a ready-for-review submission of commit `660b4b1` (fix: Correct Image.Width/Height DefaultValue metadata). Please close one as duplicate.

## Customer Impact

- Metadata consumers that read `Image.Width`/`Height` defaults via `TypeDescriptor`/`PropertyDescriptor.Attributes` no longer receive a Boolean default for `int` properties.
- Fixes `InvalidCastException` in metadata/schema consumers such as OpenAPI generation (`Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi` `ApplyDefaultValue` path).
- No runtime behavior change: property values, API surface unchanged; only design-time metadata corrected.

## Regression?

- No. This corrects invalid design-time metadata; property values and API surface are unchanged.

## Risk

- Low. Production change is limited to two `DefaultValue` attributes (+ netstandard stub parity) and is covered by a focused `TypeDescriptor` regression test. ApiCompat `CP0015` suppressions added intentionally; no API signature change.

## Test methodology

- Built `System.Drawing.Common` and `System.Drawing.Common.Tests` with the repo-pinned .NET 11 toolchain.
- New regression test `ImageTests.ImageDimensionProperty_DefaultValueIsZero` (2 cases, Width + Height): 2 passed, 0 failed.
- Full `System.Drawing.Common.Tests` suite: **5292 passed, 0 failed** (xUnit, Windows x64).
- Verified fix direction: `TypeDescriptor.GetProperties(typeof(Image))["Width"/"Height"]` default is now `System.Int32 0`, not `System.Boolean false`.

## Edge cases

Issues.Title: Fix UpDown control layout when changing and resetting fonts
Issues.Body:
<!-- Please read CONTRIBUTING.md before submitting a pull request -->

Fixes #15331

## Root cause
Two issues in font-based autoscaling cause incorrect control bounds:

1. The parent’s cached autoscale factor remains available after font-change processing completes. An inheriting container, such as DomainUpDown or NumericUpDown, can reuse that stale factor when its own font changes, unexpectedly scaling its location and width.
2. Font-driven scaling skips all child container controls, assuming they will scale themselves when receiving the parent’s font-change notification. However, containers with an explicitly assigned font do not receive that notification unless required for DPI scaling. Consequently, resetting the form’s font leaves those controls at their previously scaled positions.


## Proposed changes

- Retain the parent’s autoscale factor only while processing and propagating a font change, restoring the previous factor afterward.
- Remove the cached-factor mutation from the autoscale-factor getter.
- Skip child containers during font-driven scaling only when they will receive a font-change notification and scale themselves.
- Scale containers with explicit fonts, including their descendants, through the normal recursive scaling path while preserving DPI-specific notification handling.
- Add regression coverage for both up-down controls, direct and nested parenting, inherited and explicit fonts, and different font-change/reset sequences.

## Customer Impact

- Prevents unexpected changes to the location and width of DomainUpDown and NumericUpDown when their fonts are changed after changing the form’s font.
- Ensures that controls with explicit fonts participate in parent font-based layout scaling, allowing their location and width to return appropriately when the form’s font is reset.
- Reduces manual layout correction after font edits in the WinForms Designer. No public API changes are introduced.

## Regression? 

-  No

## Risk

- Minimal

Issues.Title: [release/10.0] Add opt-in native clipboard text fallback for WPF
Issues.Body:
Fixes dotnet/wpf#11968 in conjunction with the corresponding WPF changes.

## Proposed changes

• Add an internal, default-disabled policy allowing WPF to opt into native clipboard text fallback. WinForms explicitly remains opted out.
• Compose the original managed source with a captured native OLE reader. Legacy and typed retrieval remain managed-first, with fallback restricted to Text, UnicodeText, and OEMText .
• Preserve custom-payload identity, managed format enumeration, and writes. Add six regression cases covering WinForms clipboard behavior before and after flushing.

## Customer Impact

• Enables WPF to restore Windows text synthesis when managed clipboard sources disable automatic conversion, addressing missing text availability and retrieval reported in dotnet/wpf#11968.
• Preserves existing WinForms behavior: unflushed clipboard data retains managed conversion semantics, while flushed data exposes Windows-synthesized formats.

## Regression

• Yes — supports fixing a .NET 10 WPF regression. No intentional WinForms behavior change.

## Risk

• Low for WinForms because the fallback policy remains disabled. Moderate for opted-in consumers because shared clipboard composition and retrieval paths change. Fallback is limited to plain-text formats and retains the captured proxy’s owning adapters.

Issues.Title: WinForms VB.NET Designer requires WithEvents in .NET 11 whereas the same project works in .NET 10
Issues.Body:
### Environment

Visual Studio Professional 2026 - Version: 18.11.3, 
Visual Studio Professional 2026 Insiders - Version: 12328.396, 

### .NET version

.NET11

### Did this work in a previous version of Visual Studio and/or previous .NET release?

_No response_

### Issue description

We observed a difference in WinForms VB.NET Designer behavior between .NET 10 and .NET 11.

In .NET 10, a designer-generated control declared as:

`Private Label1 As Label`

works correctly, and the project builds, runs, and loads in the WinForms Designer without issues.

However, after migrating the same project to .NET 11, the WinForms Designer reports the following error:

1>D:\Winforms\WinFormsApp2\Form1.Designer.vb(49,13): error WFO3011: Designer component member 'Label1' must support the VB event model; add WithEvents to its declaration and use Handles for its named event handlers in the user partial (https://aka.ms/winforms-warnings/wfo3011)

The issue is resolved when the control declaration is changed to:

`Friend WithEvents Label1 As Label`

We would like to understand whether this is an intentional change in the .NET 11 WinForms Designer, a stricter designer validation rule, or a regression. We would also appreciate any documentation that explains why controls that previously worked without WithEvents in .NET 10 now require WithEvents in .NET 11.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a WinForms VB.NET project targeting .NET 10.

2. Add a Label control to a form.

3. Modify the designer declaration from:

   `Friend WithEvents Label1 As Label`

   to:

   `Private Label1 As Label`

4. Verify that the project builds and runs successfully in .NET 10.

5. Upgrade the project to target .NET 11.

6. Open the form in the WinForms Designer.

7. Observe that the Designer reports the following error:

   "Designer component member 'Label1' must support the VB event model; add WithEvents to its declaration and use Handles for its named events."

8. Change the declaration back to:

   `Friend WithEvents Label1 As Label`

10. Reopen the Designer and verify that the error is resolved.

Issues.Body:
Branch [release/8.0](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/commits/release/8.0/) in `dotnet/winforms` repo can't be mirrored from GitHub to Azure [internal/release/8.0](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_git/dotnet-winforms?version=GBinternal%2Frelease%2F8.0&_a=history) via internal merge. 

There are conflicting commits in the target branch.
The branch is configured to be mirrored via automated merge. 
The situation is rare but normal. The target branch is expected to receive manual commits in the Azure DevOps clone, which could cause conflict.

Conflicts need to be **resolved to unblock the code flow**.

- you can resolve the issue by resolving the conflict in the **target branch only**. 
    - Please make sure that the changes sensitive from security perspective are not published ahead of time to GitHub!
- reverting the extra commits in the Azdo target branch.
- checking the logs of the mirroring process in the [mirroring pipeline](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_build?definitionId=1387).
- you can disable the mirroring of the branch in the [configuration file](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_git/dotnet-mirroring?path=/dnceng-subscriptions.jsonc).
- you can ask @dotnet/dnceng for help or read the [documentation](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_git/dotnet-mirroring?path=/README.md).

Please close this issue once the conflict is resolved.
